newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs end slow day easier.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs end slow day easier.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts tended lower in slow pre-weekend trade on Friday following a lacklustre local market performance earlier, traders said.

They said the market was attracting little interest amid current political uncertainty, and was unlikely to show much change until an April 11 confidence vote on the coalition government of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
They said the key factor affecting sentiment was the likely future of the 1997/8 budget, which has not yet been passed by government.
Traders said the announcement that the investment limit for foreign funds had been raised to 30 percent from 24 percent, as set out in the budget, had little effect on sentiment.
Key prices were mixed, with SBI shedding 21 cents to $20.00/$20.75, and Indian Hotels climbing 60 cents to $21.25/$22.25. New issue VSNL was 32 cents off at $17.00/75.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.30 points, or 0.41 percent, down at 73.37 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.91 percent from 18.17 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index slipped 9.28 points to 3,550.37.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.68 points, or 1.12 percent, up at 60.90, a premium of 25.32 percent over the local market.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.19 points, or 0.15 percent, at 124.60, a discount of 5.88 percent.
